bandReport.notes:
COVERAGE. 21 items, 24-44, contiguous, no skips. Item 24 opens at the very top of p12-c1 and item 44 closes above the p20 footer, so nothing runs into p10 or p22 and neither boundary item is split. Every page carries its printed footer (13-A, 15-A, 17-A, 19-A, 21-A) inside the crops, which is how the tail of each page was confirmed complete. Reading order was c1 then c2 on every page; each page was additionally checked against pNN.png at half scale to confirm the item-to-column assignment, and all five agreed with the column crops. No page had to be read off the full page.

COLUMN CROPS. All five gutters were auto-detected (gutterFound true for 12/14/16/18/20). No crop is sliced through a line. Two cosmetic artefacts, neither affecting text: the c1 crops carry a thin sliver of the right column's item numbers past the rule (p12-c1 shows '26.'/'27.', p14-c1 '31.'/'32.', p18-c1 '38.'/'39.'/'40.', p20-c1 '43.'/'44.'), and the c2 crops carry a matching sliver of c1's line ends (most visible on p16-c2). Those slivers were read as belonging to the OTHER column and were not transcribed from the crop they appear in.

PAGE DENSITY. Item counts per page are uneven (3 on p16, 5 on p14 and p18) because several items are long; p14-c2 and p16-c1 in particular carry large blank gaps between items. Verified against the full-page renders that these gaps are typesetting only and hide no content.

PRINTED EMPHASIS PRESERVED. Item 26 prints 'not' in bold italic in the stem; transcribed as **not**, the convention already used in this corpus. Item 36 prints the binomial in italics; transcribed as *Rhynchostylis retusa*, matching the shipped precedent for italic binomials.

AS-PRINTED READINGS THAT LOOK WRONG AND WERE NOT CORRECTED. (a) Item 34 statement 2 prints 'Veliconda hills' - the usual spelling of that range is Velikonda. Confirmed at 2x on p16-c1; transcribed as printed. (b) Item 39 statement 2 prints 'The lake is situated in South Sudan along the eastern fringe of the Sahara desert.' Lake Turkana is in Kenya and Ethiopia, so the statement is false as printed - but it reads as a deliberately false option in a which-statements-are-correct item, not as a misprint. Confirmed at 2x on p18-c2; transcribed verbatim. (c) Item 26's stem has no noun after 'Which of the following' ('Which of the following with reference to Indian States is/are not correct ?'), and item 37's stem mixes a singular opener with a plural verb ('Which one of the following statements ... is/are correct ?'). Both printed exactly as shown. (d) Item 44 prints 'aircrafts'. As printed.

SCAN ARTEFACT, NOT PUNCTUATION. Item 27 statement 1 shows a small mark in the justified word gap before 'protection' on p12-c2, which reads like a stray middle dot at page scale. Enlarged 2x it is a scan speck on the paper, not a printed glyph, so it is not transcribed. Flagging it because it is visible in the crop and a later reader may take it for a raised dot.

NEAR-IDENTICAL OPTIONS IN ITEM 38 - CHECKED, NOT A DEFECT. Options (a) and (b) are word-for-word identical except for the final word ('better ocean' vs 'better life'), and (b) and (c) differ only in their first pair ('Better production' vs 'Better coral reefs'). All four are distinct as printed, so there is no duplicate-option defect - but the margin is one word, so this is the item in the band where a transcription slip would be hardest to see downstream. Re-read at 1.9x off p18-c2 specifically to confirm the four final words are ocean / life / life / mangrove vegetation and the three leading pairs are production / production / coral reefs / estuaries.

TERMINAL PUNCTUATION IN STATEMENT LISTS. Items 28, 30 and 34 print their numbered statements as phrases with NO closing full stop; items 24, 25, 26, 27, 32, 33, 36, 37, 39, 41, 42, 43 and 44 print theirs as sentences WITH one. Both reproduced as printed rather than normalised either way.

OTHER. No shared passages or Directions blocks anywhere in this band - every item is standalone, so no 'context' field is used. No item prints a List-I/List-II or any other two-column pair list, so this band contains no tables. No duplicate option texts were found. No item was unreadable. One item of the paper was dropped by UPSC; per instruction no attempt was made to guess which, and every item found on these pages is transcribed.

SUBTOPIC WARNINGS TO EXPECT. Item 26 is an India-domestic state-borders item filed under Geography > World Regional Geography > 'Landlocked and Bordering States' - the subtopic is the literal fit but the chapter name says 'World Regional', so this may warrant a catalog note. Item 43 (stealth technology) is filed under Physics rather than Defence because all three statements test electromagnetic physics (radar cross-section, radar absorbing material, metamaterials, scattering); item 44 (black boxes) is filed under Physics > Mechanics and Properties of Matter > 'Instrumentation' for the same reason.
